diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The explicit depends_on on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant: the module already depends on it via the attribute reference logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name.

The explicit depends_on on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant: aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda already depends on the module via the attribute reference arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn.

The scheduled EventBridge rule (cron every 10 minutes) will invoke the Lambda as soon as the target is attached, but nothing orders aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda after aws_lambda_permission.forge_trust_validator_lambda. Without the lambda:InvokeFunction permission for events.amazonaws.com in place, the first scheduled invocations after an apply are rejected with AccessDenied. The target should wait for the permission (e.g. depends_on = [aws_lambda_permission.forge_trust_validator_lambda]); no attribute on the target references the permission, so a bare depends_on is needed.
